title: One-Tape Configuration Embedding
statement: Let $l$ be a natural number, let $S$ and $H$ be types, choose a tape slot in $	ext{Fin}(l)$, a state map $e:S\to H$, a family of Boolean words on the $l$ host tapes, and Boolean words $w,u$ and a state $q\in S$. Embedding the one-tape configuration with input $w$, state $q$, and tape contents $u$ into the chosen slot, using the given words on all other tapes and placing every head at the origin, then renaming the state by $e$, gives the canonical configuration with state $e(q)$ and tape words obtained by replacing the chosen slot's word by $u$.
hypotheses_covered: Family of Boolean words on $l$ tapes
replaced:
For a host slot, a host word layout, a physical input $w$, a word $u$, and a
state $q$, relocating the canonical one-word configuration of a single-tape
phase (state $q$, word $u$) into that slot, with every other tape holding its
layout word at head position $0$, yields the canonical host configuration
whose layout equals the given layout with the slot's word replaced by $u$.
